name: Peridot-Null
description: Peridot-Null is a tiny barren asteroid-like body, a rough sphere of olivine-rich rock that glints pale green in reflected starlight. Impact craters cover every meter of its surface, overlapping in chaotic profusion, and solar wind has polished the surviving ridgelines to a glassy smoothness. The negligible gravity means that a strong jump would achieve escape velocity, and loose surface material drifts upward at the slightest disturbance.

Standing on Peridot-Null feels less like standing on a world and more like clinging to a large rock in open space. There is no horizon in any meaningful sense, the curvature visible in every direction. The green-tinted surface catches light in unexpected ways, and the temperature extremes between sunlit and shadowed faces can exceed three hundred degrees within a few steps.

Peridot-Null has no history worth recording. It occupies a stable orbit in an otherwise unremarkable system, too small to have differentiated, too cold to have any geological activity, and too barren to attract any attention. Automated surveys have noted its olivine composition and moved on. It is a rock, nothing more, distinguished only by the accident of its mineral content.

In the grand catalog of worlds, Peridot-Null exists as a statistical entry, a data point confirming that small olivine-rich bodies exist in this region of space. No claim has been filed, no expedition has landed, and no one has named it anything other than its survey designation, which itself has been retroactively replaced by the more evocative Peridot-Null. It will endure long after the civilizations that ignore it have turned to dust.
